candidates.attacker_control: An authenticated low-privileged administrator controls the target realm path and can issue GET /admin/realms/{realm}. The attacker's bearer token and assigned view-realm app role drive the authorization decision; no additional server-side input is needed to obtain the representation.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The endpoint is not unauthenticated: a valid bearer token is required. Some deployments could have a null private key, but default realm creation generates one and the same response leaks other credentials regardless. The admin UI describes the realm key page as the public key and the top-level realm listing gives view-realm only a minimal representation, which supports treating private-key disclosure as outside the intended view permission. No runtime request was made, and the exact downstream acceptance of forged tokens was not tested.
candidates.impact: A view-only realm administrator can steal the realm RSA signing key. With that key the attacker can mint realm-audience JWTs and identity tokens for arbitrary subjects, potentially impersonating users to adapters and, if existing session-state checks can be satisfied, to the admin API itself. The response also exposes SMTP passwords, social-provider secrets, and user-federation configuration, enabling further credential compromise.
candidates.prerequisites: The requester must have a valid admin bearer token and a user or client role mapping that satisfies view-realm for the target realm. The admin REST endpoint must be reachable. Default realm creation generates an RSA key pair, so the private key is normally present.
candidates.root_cause: RealmAdminResource.getRealm authorizes the request with RealmAuth.hasView(), so the view-realm role is sufficient, and then returns ModelToRepresentation.toRepresentation(realm). That conversion unconditionally copies realm.getPrivateKeyPem() into the response representation, along with SMTP, social-provider, and federation configuration. There is no manage-realm requirement and no stripping of private or secret fields.
candidates.title: Read-only realm administrator can retrieve the realm private signing key
candidates.trace: AdminRoot authenticates the bearer token without requiring a manage role -> RealmsAdminResource.getRealmAdmin creates RealmAdminResource/RealmAuth -> GET getRealm calls auth.hasView() -> RealmAuth.hasView() accepts view-realm or manage-realm -> ModelToRepresentation.toRepresentation copies realm.getPrivateKeyPem() and secret maps into RealmRepresentation -> Jackson serializes the public getPrivateKey() value. As counterpoint, RealmsAdminResource.addRealmRep only includes the full representation for manage-realm and gives view-realm a name-only representation, so the direct endpoint is the inconsistent stronger path.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed. The deployed realm's key presence and the full downstream token/session acceptance chain were inferred from source. The P1 index has no data-flow or semantic resolution, so the call/serialization path was verified by reading the Java source rather than by an execution trace.
candidates.weakness_type: Improper authorization / exposure of sensitive information (CWE-863, CWE-200)

coverage_summary: Reviewed the visible 1,259-file snapshot, focusing on admin REST authorization, realm/application/client secret representations, OIDC/OAuth token and redirect handling, SAML and social flows, account/login actions, theme/resource serving, JPA/Mongo and LDAP federation, adapters, crypto/JWS, configuration, and export/import. The P1 index is partial: 1,239 files indexed, 739 Java files parsed, 20 source files missing from the index, 21,162 syntactic edges and 12,582 unresolved calls; its control-flow and data-flow analyses are explicitly unavailable. The candidate path was verified against source text rather than relying on index labels. No build, tests, scanners, or runtime requests were executed.
limitations: The relation index is syntactic and partial: 20 files are absent, and no control-flow, data-flow, semantic resolution, or exploitability proof is available.
No runtime, build, or test evidence was collected; framework path normalization, deployed configuration, and token acceptance were not exercised.
The review was broad but not an exhaustive line-by-line audit of all 1,259 files, especially documentation, examples, tests, generated assets, and dependency internals.
Some security-relevant behavior is delegated to external libraries such as PicketLink, RESTEasy, Jackson, and the servlet container; those implementations were not inspected or executed.
The candidate requires a privileged-but-read-only realm administrator and was not confirmed against a live deployment.

rejected_leads.lead: Folder theme path traversal in FolderTheme.getResource
rejected_leads.reason: The path is concatenated under a resources directory without canonical-path containment, but exploitability depends on container-level dot-segment/encoded-slash normalization and the deployed filesystem theme layout; not selected without runtime verification.

origin is inserted unescaped into JavaScript, but the request only passes validation when a client is configured with a wildcard web origin or an exact matching origin; no source proves that configuration is present.
RelayState is written into HTML without escaping and could be reflected XSS, but it requires an enabled SAML client and signature policy/flow conditions that were not verified.

rejected_leads.lead: RealmAdminResource.deleteSession lacks an explicit RealmAuth check
rejected_leads.reason: This is a real-looking missing authorization check, but session IDs are high-entropy and the direct demonstrated effect is limited to session termination/DoS unless another source leaks the session ID.

rejected_leads.lead: LoginActionsService.Checks.check does not return false after a failed requiredAction check
rejected_leads.reason: The signed code still binds the session, and the apparent bypass generally affects the same user session or self-service action; no cross-user escalation was established.

rejected_leads.lead: Token type confusion between access and refresh tokens
rejected_leads.reason: Token parsing and refresh handling do not clearly enforce the REFRESH type, but exploitation requires possession of a valid signed token and the practical impact is lower than the realm-key disclosure.

summary: The strongest source-supported candidate is an authorization-boundary failure in the admin realm API: a user with only the read-only `view-realm` role can retrieve a full realm representation that includes the realm RSA private signing key and other secret configuration. The top-level realm listing deliberately returns only a minimal representation to non-`manage-realm` users, while the direct realm GET returns the full representation whenever `hasView()` is true, indicating the private-key exposure is unintended. Other suspicious leads were left unconfirmed rather than split into additional candidates.
